surface_mechanism_description: The carbon atoms are selectively adsorbed on surface gallium atoms, and arsine removes the carbon atoms from the growth surface. The exchange interaction between carbon atoms on the surface and arsenic atoms in the lattice plays a role in the incorporation of carbon.
evidence: The carbon concentration was found to increase in the saturation region, as shown in figs. 4 and 5. This indicates that the carbon contamination does not directly come from TMG adsorbed on arsenic site, but from the hydrocarbon or carbon in the vapor. The number of hydrocarbon molecules or carbon atoms in the vapor is considered to be proportional to the mole fraction or the pulse duration of TMG. The carbon concentration N c in a film can be expressed as ... The upper curve in fig. 4 was calculated from eq. (1) using the assumption of selective adsorption, i.e., assuming that rc.As was infinitely large. When the value of rc.As was finite and comparable to rc.Ga, the observed sharp drop of hole concentration for small values of TMG mole fraction could not be reproduced by eq. (1) at all. This indicates that adsorption of hydrocarbon or carbon takes place selectively on surface gallium atoms. Arsine plays an important role in the incorporation of carbon. The film had a high impurity concentration, above 3 × 1018 cm-3 when insufficient arsine was supplied to the surface (fig. 6). Observations showed that as the arsine pulse duration increased, the carbon concentration decreased. It is thus concluded that the arsine removes the carbon atoms from the growth surface. The exchange interaction between the carbon atoms on the surface and the arsenic atoms in the lattice plays an important role in this reaction.
